summary: Frontend retest after script load-order fix. Iteration 1's critical script-order bug is RESOLVED — main.js now loads before admin.js / forms.js in rendered HTML (lines 276 vs 278). All 12 frontend flows pass EXCEPT PDF download for invoices that have no candidate (a NEW backend bug surfaced by the new-invoice modal which does not capture a candidate). Specifically: auth-guard redirect, login, KPI population, all 6 admin tabs, candidate drawer + status save, new invoice creation, mark-paid, logout, and all three public forms (candidate/company/contact) submit via fetch and show .form-note.is-success. The only failure is /api/admin/invoices/<id>/pdf returning 500 for the freshly-created invoice (candidate_name is NULL in DB → reportlab AttributeError).

critical.issue: Returns 500 (text/html) when the invoice row has candidate_name=NULL. Traceback: File /app/backend/invoice.py line 102 → reportlab/platypus/paragraph.py → AttributeError: 'NoneType' object has no attribute 'split'. Root cause: `invoice.get('candidate_name', '—')` returns None (not '—') because the key exists but its value is NULL. Same risk applies to any other field passed to Paragraph(...) without a None-guard. Fix: use `invoice.get('candidate_name') or '—'` (and same for company_name, role, etc.). PDF works fine on the iteration-1 seeded invoice where candidate_name is set.

integration_issues.issue: The new-invoice modal only captures company + placement_fee + GST. It does NOT collect candidate_name (no candidate selector / placement reference). The created row in invoices table therefore has candidate_name=NULL in the DB, which in turn triggers the PDF 500 above. Either (a) require selecting a placement / candidate in the modal, or (b) auto-fill from the company's most recent placement, or (c) keep optional but fix the PDF None-guard. Test spec did not require entering a candidate, so the backend fix is the more conservative path.

action_items: Fix /app/backend/invoice.py None-handling: replace `invoice.get('candidate_name', '—')` with `invoice.get('candidate_name') or '—'` (and audit every other Paragraph(...) call that pulls from invoice dict — company_name, role, hr_name etc. — to use the `or '—'` pattern). After the fix, PDF download for the newly-created invoice should return application/pdf.
Optional UX: extend the new-invoice modal to optionally pick a placement/candidate so candidate_name is populated at creation time.

rca of the issue: Bug: PDF generation crashes with AttributeError for invoices whose candidate_name column is NULL. Reproduction: login as admin → Invoices → '+ Generate invoice' → pick company → enter placement_fee=100000 → submit. New row appears with candidate_name=NULL. Click PDF on that row → /api/admin/invoices/<id>/pdf returns 500 (text/html). Root cause: /app/backend/invoice.py line 102 calls `Paragraph(invoice.get('candidate_name', '—'), body)`. dict.get(key, default) returns the default ONLY when key is MISSING — when key exists with value None, it returns None. reportlab.Paragraph then calls .split() on None → AttributeError. Mitigation: change to `Paragraph(invoice.get('candidate_name') or '—', body)` and audit all sibling fields in invoice.py for the same anti-pattern. Optional FE mitigation: make the new-invoice modal require a placement/candidate selection so candidate_name is never NULL at insert time.
